blockNote: Event block tile system — runtime map edits (doors, bridges, barriers) driven by event flags (172521–173533, Bank 02).

An event block copies a rectangle of map tiles from a source position over a destination position, either instantly (SwapEventBlockTiles) or animated with VRAM updates (AnimateEventBlock). Despite its name SwapEventBlockTiles does not exchange the two rectangles: the source is left unchanged.
=== EVENT FLAG INDEXING ===

ApplyAllEventBlocks walks the 32-byte event flag bitfield at $0A20 (LSR per bit). For every set flag the event index ($04, 8-bit, wraps after 256 indices) goes through LookupEventBlock; when the scene matches, SwapEventBlockTiles runs. Callers: scene_lifecycle and inventory_overlay. Defeated-enemy blocks call LookupEventBlock + SwapEventBlockTiles from actor_execution; COP #32 StageBgChange calls LookupEventBlock and COP #33 ApplyBgChange loops AnimateEventBlock.
=== EVENT BLOCK TABLE FORMAT ===
LookupEventBlock reads 8-byte entries from event_block_table (index × 8) into WRAM $0096-$00A8 (absolute addresses, used as DP with D = 0):
Byte 0: Scene ID — must match sceneCurrent or the entry is skipped (carry set = no match)
Bytes 1-2: Source tile X/Y ($96/$98)
Byte 3: Width ($A2, and $9E as the column counter); byte 4: height ($A0)
Bytes 5-6: Destination tile X/Y ($9A/$9C)
Byte 7: Layer flag ($A4) — 0 = layer 0 (mapLayerTilemap + collisionLayer), nonzero = layer 1 (effectLayerTilemap)
$A8 keeps the entry's byte offset so AdvanceEventRow can reload the start X coordinates.
=== TILE COPY OPERATIONS ===

1. SwapEventBlockTiles (instant): nested row/column loop using map_coords.MapIndexMoveRight/MapIndexMoveDown. Layer 0 copies the mapLayerTilemap and collisionLayer bytes. Layer 1 copies effectLayerTilemap and looks the collision byte up through the [$3E] pointer (base $06AC, low byte replaced by the tile ID, bank $7F); the collision byte is written only when the lookup is non-zero.

2. AnimateEventBlock (animated): same copy, but each copied tile that is inside the camera window also queues a 2×2 metatile VRAM update. Layer 0 queues through QueueVisibleTileVram (BG1 nametable) and, when the queue is full, flushes inside the routine (UpdateFrameDialogue) and restarts; layer 1 has its own inline copy of the visibility and queue code (BG2 nametable, $0800 offset) and instead returns carry clear when the queue is full so the caller (COP #33) flushes a frame and calls again. Carry set = all tiles done.
=== VRAM WRITE QUEUE ($0800-$08FF) ===

A queue entry is a pair of words (VRAM word address, tile word); one 2×2 metatile is four entries = $10 bytes, so the queue holds 16 metatiles (Y = $0100 = full). The queue's first word is dmaSkipFlag ($0800): nonzero means entries are pending. A zero address word terminates the list; both animate paths write that terminator at $0800+Y.
FlushVramWriteQueue (called twice from system_core's frame update) has two modes:
- Queued mode (dmaSkipFlag nonzero): SP is pointed at $07FF so PLA pops address/tile pairs straight into VMADDL/VMDATAL until the zero terminator; dmaSkipFlag is cleared afterwards.

- Direct mode (dmaSkipFlag zero): if tileQueryResult ($0902, really the VRAM address of a pending 2×2 metatile update staged by cop_handlers_metatile) is nonzero, writes its two tile rows ($0904/$0906 at $0902, $090A/$090C at $0908), then clears it.
=== VISIBILITY CHECK ===

A tile is queued only when its pixel position is inside the camera window: (pixelX + 16 − scrollH) < $0111 and (pixelY − ((scrollV − 16) AND $FFF0)) in 0..$F0. Layer 0 and QueueVisibleTileVram use bg1ScrollH / mapScrollV; the layer 1 path uses effectScrollH / effectScrollV.

QueueVisibleTileVram contract: carry set = off-screen (nothing queued); carry clear and Z set = queue full (the LDX #0 exists only to force Z); carry clear on success, where Z is whatever the caller's flags were (PLP restores them, OQ-62). DrawChestTiles in warps_interaction is its other caller and ignores the result.
=== HELPER ROUTINES ===
AdvanceEventColumn: decrements the column counter ($9E); carry set when the row is done, otherwise pixel X += 16, source/destination tile X += 1 and both map indices step right.

AdvanceEventRow: decrements the row counter ($A0); carry set when all rows are done, otherwise pixel Y += 16, tile Y += 1 (both), source X and destination X are reloaded from the original table entry ($A8) and the column counter is reset from $A2.

ApplyAllEventBlocks: Apply every active event block for the current scene.

Walks the event flag bitfield at $0A20 in 8-bit chunks (LSR shifts each flag into carry). For each set flag the event index ($04) goes through LookupEventBlock; when the scene matches (carry clear), SwapEventBlockTiles copies the rectangle instantly. The outer loop ends when $04 wraps to zero (256 indices, 32 bytes).
Saves and restores processor state (PHP/PLP). The bitfield loop is 8-bit; the lookup call switches to 16-bit.
SwapEventBlockTiles: Copy a rectangle of tiles from the source position over the destination position (the source is not modified, so this is a copy, not a swap).

Entry: parameters at WRAM $0096-$00A4 as loaded by LookupEventBlock, read through DP with D = 0: $96/$98 source X/Y tile, $9A/$9C destination X/Y tile, $9E columns remaining, $A0 rows remaining, $A2 original width, $A4 layer flag (0 = layer 0, nonzero = layer 1).

Layer 0 path (loc_02A264): per tile, copies mapLayerTilemap and collisionLayer bytes from the source map index ($02) to the destination index ($00); MapIndexMoveRight/MapIndexMoveDown traverse the rectangle.

Layer 1 path (loc_02A2B9): same traversal on effectLayerTilemap. The collision byte comes from an indirect lookup: $3E/$40 hold the collision flag table pointer ($06AC, bank $7F) and the tile ID replaces the low byte of $3E, so [$3E] returns the table entry for that tile. The collision byte is written only if the entry is non-zero (empty overlay tiles keep the existing collision).
FlushVramWriteQueue: Write queued tile updates to VRAM during VBlank.

1. Queued mode (dmaSkipFlag nonzero): saves SP, sets SP = $07FF so the first PLA reads word $0800 (dmaSkipFlag itself, the first queued VRAM address). Pops address/tile pairs (PLA → VMADDL, PLA → VMDATAL) until a zero address word, then restores SP and clears dmaSkipFlag.

2. Direct mode (dmaSkipFlag zero): VMAIN = $80 (word access, increment after the high byte). If $0902 (tileQueryResult) is nonzero it is the VRAM address of the top row of a 2×2 metatile: tile words $0904/$0906 go there, then $090A/$090C go to the address in $0908. $0902 is cleared afterwards (it is also cleared when it was already zero).
AnimateEventBlock: Animated event block copy: same rectangle copy as SwapEventBlockTiles, but every copied tile inside the camera window also queues a 2×2 metatile VRAM update so the change appears progressively.

Layer 0 path (loc_02A3EF): copies mapLayerTilemap + collisionLayer, calls QueueVisibleTileVram with pixel positions $1A (X) / $1E (Y). Carry set (off-screen) advances to the next tile. Z set with carry clear (queue full) advances, writes the zero terminator at $0800+Y, calls UpdateFrameDialogue so the NMI flushes the queue, and restarts from the current tile with Y = 0.

Layer 1 path (code_02A443): copies effectLayerTilemap, resolves collision through [$3E] like SwapEventBlockTiles, and has its own inline visibility test (effectScrollH / effectScrollV) and queue code (metatileEffectLayer, VRAM address + $0800). When its queue fills and tiles remain it writes the terminator and returns carry clear: the caller must flush a frame and call again.

Returns carry set when every tile has been processed (terminator written), carry clear when interrupted by a full layer 1 queue. Uses DP = 0 and keeps all progress in $96-$A8, so a repeated call resumes where it stopped.
QueueVisibleTileVram: Queue the 2×2 metatile VRAM update for the tile at pixel position ($1A, $1E) if it is inside the camera window. Layer 0 only: X = map index of the tile in mapLayerTilemap, Y = queue offset (JSR, same bank).
Window test: (pixelX + 16 − bg1ScrollH) < $0111, and (pixelY − ((mapScrollV − 16) AND $FFF0)) in 0..$F0.

On-screen: reads the mapLayerTilemap byte, ×8 indexes metatileMapLayer ($7E2000), copies its four tile words to $0802/$0806/$080A/$080E + Y, and stores PixelToVramAddress (BG1 nametable) and the +1 / +$20 / +$21 neighbours as the four address words ($0800/$0804/$0808/$080C + Y). Y advances by $10 per metatile.

Returns: carry set = off-screen; carry clear + Z set = queue full (Y reached $0100, LDX #0 forces Z); carry clear otherwise (Z is inherited from the caller's flags, OQ-62). Also used by DrawChestTiles in warps_interaction.
AdvanceEventRow: Advance to the next row of the event block rectangle.

Decrements the row counter ($A0); carry set (SEC) when all rows are done. Otherwise: pixel Y ($1E) += 16, source ($98) and destination ($9C) tile Y += 1, source X ($96) and destination X ($9A) are reloaded from the original event_block_table entry (offset kept in $A8, bytes +1 and +5), and the column counter ($9E) is reset from the width ($A2). Returns carry clear (more rows).

blockNote: Hardware math utilities — SNES multiplication and division using the 5A22 math registers (163840–164464, Bank 02).

Wrappers around the hardware multiplier ($4202/$4203 → $4216/$4217, unsigned 8×8) and divider ($4204/$4205/$4206 → $4214/$4216, unsigned 16÷8). Results need NOP delays (8 machine cycles after a multiply, 16 after a divide).
=== ROUTINES ===

MulDivide: (A low × Y) ÷ A high. A low = multiplier, A high = divisor, Y = 16-bit multiplicand. Two 8×8 multiplies (A low × Y low, A low × Y high) are combined into the 16-bit dividend: the product's low 16 bits only — anything above bit 15 is discarded, so the product must fit in 16 bits. A divisor of 0 gives $FFFF. Returns the 16-bit quotient. Users: camera_scroll, parallax_thinker, visual_effect_pipeline.

SignedMultiply: 8×8 multiply with the operands in the two bytes of A (low = first, high = second), through long addresses ($80:4202/4203/4216/4217) so any data bank works. Returns the 16-bit product in A. The hardware multiplier is unsigned, so despite the name this is an unsigned multiply (see rename proposal 84). Used for index × $30 actor addressing, map index calculation, orbital offsets and others.
UnsignedDivide: 16÷8 divide. Y = 16-bit dividend, A = 8-bit divisor. Returns the quotient's low byte in A low and the remainder in A high (the quotient's high byte is dropped).
SoftDivide_Unused: software long division, no callers.
IncrementCounter_Unused: standalone copy of the generator step that RngByte (cop_handlers_movement) runs inline; no callers.

MulDivide: Multiply then divide with the hardware registers: (A low × Y) ÷ A high.
Input: A = packed operand (low byte = multiplier, high byte = divisor), Y = 16-bit multiplicand.

Algorithm: P1 = A low × Y low and P2 = A low × Y high (two 8×8 multiplies). The dividend is the 16-bit value P1 + (P2 low byte << 8): the carry out and P2's high byte are discarded, so only the low 16 bits of A low × Y are divided. The divisor is A high; WRDIVB triggers the divide.
Output: 16-bit quotient in A (RDDIVL/RDDIVH). Divisor 0 returns $FFFF (hardware behaviour).
Timing: 3 NOPs after the multiplies (plus the instructions between), 8 NOPs (16 cycles) after the divide.
SignedMultiply: 8×8 multiply through long-address hardware registers (named SignedMultiply, but the $4202/$4203 multiplier is unsigned).
Input: A low = first operand, A high = second operand (8-bit accumulator). STA $80:4202, XBA, STA $80:4203.
Output: 16-bit product in A (high byte from $80:4217 via XBA, low byte from $80:4216).
Long addresses make it independent of the current data bank.
UnsignedDivide: Input: Y = 16-bit dividend (WRDIVL/WRDIVH), A = 8-bit divisor (WRDIVB, which starts the divide).
Output: A low = quotient low byte (RDDIVL), A high = remainder (RDMPYL), assembled with XBA. The quotient's high byte is not returned.
8 NOPs (16 cycles) cover the divide latency.
SoftDivide_Unused: Software long division (no callers). Uses DP = 0 scratch $00-$06. A = divisor, Y = dividend.

The divisor is normalized by shifting left until its MSB is set (shift count in $00, normalized divisor in $02). The dividend then acts as a running remainder through two trial-subtraction loops: the first collects the integer quotient bits into $06 (shift count + 1 iterations, at most 16), the second 16 further bits into $04 (a 16.16 fixed-point quotient, inferred). Probably a development fallback before the hardware divider wrapper.
IncrementCounter_Unused: Generator step (no callers); the same loops as the inline step in RngByte (cop_handlers_movement), without the output byte.

For X = 15..1: byte[$040F+X] += byte[$0410+X] + carry (one carry chain, $041E first). Then a ripple counter at $041F is incremented, carrying toward lower addresses until a byte does not wrap. The state array is $0410-$041F; rngState ($040F) is only the base used for the X offset.

blockNote: COP handlers that query the player or linked actors (Bank 00, COP #44-#49 in hex = copdef ids 68-73).

#44 BranchIfPlayerInRelTiles and #45 BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles test whether the player actor is inside a tile rectangle and branch (four bytes: minX, minY, maxX, maxY, then a &Code target). #46/#47 copy this actor's position to its previous/next linked actor. #48 GetPlayerFacing returns the player's facing in A. #49 BranchIfBodyNe branches when characterForm differs from a byte.

Rectangle tests use unsigned compares with an exclusive lower bound and an inclusive upper bound (minX < player.X ≤ maxX, same for Y). Uses in extracted/: #44 44, #45 140, #48 6; #46, #47 and #49 have no users.

BranchIfPlayerInRelTiles: COP #44 (copdef id 68): relative tile-rectangle branch. Operands: four signed bytes in the order minX, minY, maxX, maxY (tiles, relative to this actor) plus a &Code target.

Each byte is sign-extended, multiplied by 16 (ASL ×4) and added to the actor's own X ($14) or Y ($16). The player is inside when minX < player.X ≤ maxX and minY < player.Y ≤ maxY (unsigned compares on the player actor's $14/$16). Inside → jump to the target; otherwise skip the six-byte operand block (4 bytes + &Code).
BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles: COP #45 (copdef id 69): absolute tile-rectangle branch. Operands: four bytes in the order minX, minY, maxX, maxY (absolute tile coordinates) plus a &Code target.

Each byte is multiplied by 16 and compared with the player actor's position. The tested point is (player.X, player.Y − 8): inside when minX×16 < X ≤ maxX×16 and minY×16 < Y−8 ≤ maxY×16. The adjusted Y is kept in scratch $0000. Inside → jump to the target; otherwise skip the six-byte operand block.
CopyPosToPrev: COP #46 (id 70), no operands, no users. Copies this actor's pixel position ($14/$16) to its previous linked actor ($04). No null check: with no previous actor ($04 = 0) it would write to WRAM $0014/$0016.
CopyPosToNext: COP #47 (id 71), no operands, no users. Copies this actor's pixel position ($14/$16) to its next linked actor ($06); shares the copy code with CopyPosToPrev. No null check.
BranchIfBodyNe: COP #49 (id 73), no users. One byte (form ID) plus a &Code target: branches when characterForm ($0AD4) is not equal to the byte; when equal it skips the 2-byte target.

blockNote: COP handlers for actor spawning — the SpawnBefore/After/Abs/Offset/Marked family plus list append (Bank $00, 14 COP handlers, ids $99-$A6).

SpawnBefore*/SpawnAfter* call AllocateActorBefore/AllocateActorAfter, which link a new actor beside the spawner and CopyActorState (clones $0E, $10 with $2000 set, $12 without bit 12, position and more from the spawner). The handler then writes the entry address (word at $0000, bank at $0002) and any operands: position offsets are added to the inherited $14/$16, absolute positions replace them, a flags word replaces $0010.

The Marked variants (SpawnBeforeMarked, SpawnAfterMarked, SpawnAfterAbsMarked, SpawnAfterOffsetMarked) set $0040 in the spawner's own $12 (Die cascades to marked children) and call MarkChildActor, which sets the new actor's parentId to the spawner's parentId, or to the spawner itself when it has none.

SpawnListAppend/SpawnListAppendSpr use ActorPoolAllocator and append at the tail of the actor list ($0058); on pool exhaustion they skip all operand bytes without spawning. SpawnListAppendSpr also reads an animation index (stored at $0028).

Uses in extracted/: SpawnListAppend 256, SpawnAfterFlags 231, SpawnAfterOffsetFlags 126, SpawnAfterAbsFlags 106, SpawnAfterMarked 101, SpawnAfterOffsetMarked 77; SpawnAfterOffset, SpawnAfterAbs and SpawnListAppendSpr have no users.

SpawnAfterOffset: COP #9D with one Address plus two word operands (X/Y offset), no users. Spawns after the current actor and adds the 16-bit offset words to the new actor's $0014/$0016.
SpawnAfterAbs: COP #9F with one Address plus two word operands (absolute X/Y), no users. Spawns after the current actor and assigns $0014/$0016 directly from the operand words.
SpawnListAppendSpr: COP #A6 with one Address, one byte (animation index), two signed bytes (X/Y offset) and one word (flags), no users. Like SpawnListAppend but also stores the animation index in the spawned actor's $0028; the pool-exhaustion path skips one more operand byte (8 operand bytes in total).

blockNote: COP handlers for SPC700 audio communication and music playback (Bank $00, 8 COP handlers).

StartMusic (#04) allocates a thinker with AllocateActorAfter and sets its entry to SpcTransferMusicData for the asynchronous SPC upload. FadeThenStartMusic (#05) does the same but enters at SpcCheckMusicReady, an $F1/$01 handshake before the upload; no fade logic is in that routine (the name's 'fade' is unverified, OQ-61). Both OR $1000 into the thinker's $12 (it keeps running while the world is frozen, as in MusicPlaybackActor), clear $1000 in its $10 and store the track in chatPtr.

PlaySoundCh2 (#06), PlaySoundCh1 (#07) and PlaySoundBoth (#08) write the sfx queue bytes sfxQueueCh1/Ch2 ($06F8/$06F9); WriteApuIo1 (#09) and WriteApuIo0 (#0A) write APUIO1/APUIO0 ($2141/$2140) directly.

MusicAndText (#19) allocates a pooled actor with ActorPoolAllocator, appends it to the list tail, CopyActorState, sets it to MusicPlaybackActor and stores the three operands ($0026 track, $0020 text pointer, $0022 text bank). On pool exhaustion the track is dropped and only the text is shown inline through DialogStringRenderer, then displayModeFlags bit 7 is cleared.
Uses in extracted/: PlaySoundCh1 244, PlaySoundCh2 92, PlaySoundBoth 72, StartMusic 57, MusicAndText 22, FadeThenStartMusic 14, WriteApuIo0 7, WriteApuIo1 4.

StartMusic: COP #04 with one byte operand (music bundle ID). Allocates a thinker with AllocateActorAfter, sets its entry to SpcTransferMusicData, ORs $1000 into its $12 and clears $1000 in its $10 (the mask is $EFFF; it is not the $0800 render bit), and stores the music ID in chatPtr. The thinker runs the SPC handshake and upload asynchronously.
FadeThenStartMusic: COP #05 with one byte operand (music bundle ID). Same allocation, $12/$10 flag handling and chatPtr as StartMusic, but the thinker's entry is SpcCheckMusicReady: it sends $F1 on APUIO0, waits for the echo, sends $01, and falls into SpcTransferMusicData when the SPC answers zero. That routine contains no fade step (OQ-61).

blockNote: Cutscene auto-walk actors (Bank 00) spawned by warps_interaction.StartForcedWalk during extended warp transitions.

StartForcedWalk decodes the direction from scrollStepTableBase (bit 5 = west, bit 4 = east, bit 7 = north, default south), sets playerFlags $0100 and spawns the matching ForcedWalkSouth/North/West/East on the player actor (SpawnBefore).

The warp entry gives two things: the walk-step stream pointed to by warpFacing ($0650, a pointer to warp entry +7) and the walk sequence index in scrollStepTableBase. Stream layout, 6 bytes: [direction byte][X offset word][Y offset word][direction byte]. A direction byte indexes direction_velocity_table, whose entry is (animation index, index into movement_delta_table); movement_delta_table entries are delta-node lists, so ReadDirSprite_*Velocity leaves a velocity-curve pointer in $2E (Y) or $2C (X).

Each ForcedWalk* actor: masks all joypad input, reads the first direction byte, stages the player sprite (StagePlayerSprFromDP, animation index from DP $0000), replaces scrollStepTableBase with the pointer to the word scroll-step list from forced_walk_sequence_table (read by CameraScrollStepLookup, ends at a zero word), pans the camera in the walk direction (CameraPan*), adds the stream's X/Y offset words to its own position (ApplyScrollOffset), reads the second direction byte, stages the final sprite, copies position and state to the player (SyncPlayerToCamera), unmasks the joypad and dies.
The direction variants differ only in the ReadDirSprite helper (Y velocity for south/north, X for west/east) and the CameraPan* COP.

ForcedWalkSouth: Cutscene auto-walk actor spawned on the player by StartForcedWalk during extended warp transitions (default direction when no west/east/north bit is set).

Masks all joypad input, reads the first stream direction byte with ReadDirSprite_YVelocity, stages the player sprite, loads the walk sequence pointer from forced_walk_sequence_table into scrollStepTableBase, pans the camera down (CameraPanDown), applies the stream's position offset, reads the next direction byte, re-stages the sprite, syncs the player and dies. The North/West/East labels below follow the same sequence.
ForcedWalkNorth: Same sequence as ForcedWalkSouth with ReadDirSprite_YVelocity and CameraPanUp.
ForcedWalkWest: Same sequence as ForcedWalkSouth with ReadDirSprite_XVelocity and CameraPanLeft.
ForcedWalkEast: Same sequence as ForcedWalkSouth with ReadDirSprite_XVelocity and CameraPanRight.
ReadDirSprite_YVelocity: Read the next walk-step stream byte and set up the sprite and the Y velocity curve for it.

Y = stream pointer (warpFacing, $0650), incremented by one. The byte indexes direction_velocity_table (word entries): the whole word goes to $0000 (low byte = animation index used by StagePlayerSprFromDP); its high byte indexes movement_delta_table, and that pointer (head of a delta-node velocity list) is stored in $2E. ReadDirSprite_XVelocity is identical but stores it in $2C.
ReadDirSprite_XVelocity: Same as ReadDirSprite_YVelocity, but the velocity-curve pointer goes to $2C (X axis) instead of $2E.
ApplyScrollOffset: Add the next stream record, an X word and a Y word, to this actor's position ($14/$16); the stream pointer ($0650) advances by 4.
SyncPlayerToCamera: Copy this actor's final state to the player actor: position ($14/$16), animation index ($28), $10 with $0008 set and $0200 cleared (OQ-60), and zero the player's $08.
